title: Commodities Brief — 14 Aug 2026
intro:
Agriculture markets surge on weather-driven supply concerns while precious metals hold elevated levels amid persistent geopolitical premium. Energy complex stabilizes with crude pushing higher on tightening inventory data, though natural gas remains pressured by weak seasonal demand.
🥇 PRECIOUS METALS
Gold $4389.90 +0.60% | Bias: LONG | Key levels: $4350 support / $4450 resistance. Price consolidating near all-time highs with geopolitical risk premium intact. Silver $64.51 -0.55% underperforming as gold-silver ratio widens to 68, presenting tactical long opportunity on ratio compression. Platinum $1723.60 -0.09% trading sideways, industrial demand outlook mixed. Palladium $1306.50 -1.22% extending weekly decline on automotive sector softness.

sections.heading: ⚡ ENERGY
sections.content:
WTI $82.66 +1.74% | Bias: BULLISH | Key levels: $80.50 / $85.00. Brent $88.36 +1.48% gaining momentum on Middle East supply risk and stronger-than-expected Chinese import data. Brent-WTI spread at $5.70 reflects tight North American pipeline capacity and export constraints. Natural Gas $2.75 +0.81% bouncing intraday but down 1.61% on settlement, trapped below $3.00 resistance as mild weather forecasts limit cooling demand.
🌾 AGRICULTURE
Wheat $679.25 +4.06% accelerating on Black Sea export disruption reports and deteriorating North American spring crop conditions. Corn $477.00 +6.47% leading gains as USDA cuts yield estimates following Midwest drought stress. Soybeans $1190.00 +1.86% supported by strong crush margins and South American production concerns.

sections.heading: 🎯 TRADE IDEAS
sections.content:
LONG: Corn - momentum continuation on supply cuts - entry $475 - SL $465 - TP $495
LONG: WTI Crude - technical breakout above $82 with inventory support - entry $82.50 - SL $80.00 - TP $87.00
SHORT: Palladium - automotive weakness persists, break below support - entry $1305 - SL $1335 - TP $1250

sections.heading: ⚠️ RISKS
sections.content:
Dollar strength reversal could pressure all commodities if Fed signals earlier rate cuts are off the table.
Weather pattern shifts favoring crop development would quickly deflate agriculture rally and trigger profit-taking.
